name: Menu Boards
title: Menu Boards: operator and guest paths and what can go wrong

BANDS.s: Module and permissions switched on, dongle or TV bought, powered and booted

BANDS.t: Install app and map the device
BANDS.s: Menu board app installed and kept updated, device registered as a TV for one restaurant
Playlists page: name, orientation, images, videos, legacy templates and canvas boards in order with durations

BANDS.t: Design a board in the canvas editor
BANDS.s: Canvas editor: size, background, text, media, shapes, menu blocks, modifiers, fonts and brand book
Autosave and manual save of the board JSON, then preview in the editor and on the Playlists page
Screens page: pick playlists for each TV, order them and set day and time schedules
Cache invalidation, the TV app fetching its screen data and caching it
The TV renders the board, cycles the playlist, applies schedules and stock and survives a full day
Prices, items, stock, menu timings and business hours changed in other products and reaching the board
Changing or deleting playlists and items, removing a TV, moving or churning a restaurant

NODES.d: The restaurant signs up for digital menu boards. AIO ships an Android dongle per TV or uses an Android TV, and the onboarding team plans how many screens, which orientation and which content.
e: Number of TVs, orientation and resolution not captured at sale, boards designed for the wrong shape
Restaurant TVs are not Android capable and no dongle is shipped

NODES.d: Menu Board is a tenant module with its own permissions (playlists create and view, screens). Owner and Manager default roles include them. The Web Dash sidebar shows the Menu Boards group with Screens and Playlists only when the module and permission are on.
e: Module not enabled for the tenant, sidebar group missing and the operator cannot find the feature
Custom roles created before the module lack the menu board permissions, staff see an empty or blocked page
Only one permission gates the canvas editor route, any user who can create playlists can also overwrite every board
No separation of design and approval

NODES.d: The dongle is plugged into the TV HDMI port and a USB or mains power supply, boots Android and the launcher, then joins the restaurant Wi-Fi.
e: The menu board dongle does not power on
Screen dark, no menu for guests
The dongle boots into Android recovery instead of showing the menu
Board down until the dongle is replaced or reflashed
TV input not set to the dongle HDMI port or TV sleep timer turns the panel off
Launcher does not auto-start the menu board app after a reboot
Staff must open the app every morning
No spare dongle or remote replacement process, a failed unit takes days to replace
Long outage on a paid feature

NODES.d: The dongle needs internet to fetch its screen data and media. There is no wired option on most dongles.
e: Dongle behind the TV gets weak Wi-Fi signal, media downloads time out
Guest or captive portal network used, the app cannot reach the API
Wi-Fi password changed by the restaurant, every dongle drops offline with no alert to anyone

NODES.d: The React Native menu board app is sideloaded onto the dongle, outside the Play Store, and later updates itself.
e: An old build is installed from an unknown source at setup, the device starts on v1.0 instead of the current version
No record of which app version each dongle runs, support cannot tell old from new devices
Unknown sources or install permission blocked on the device

NODES.d: The app checks for a newer build and installs it without the Play Store. Mechanism not in this repo.
e: Auto-update does not run, device stays on v1.0 while the fleet is on v6.0
Old behaviour such as wrong closed state
Update downloaded on weak Wi-Fi is corrupted or half installed, app will not open
Update restarts the app during service with no schedule control
No forced minimum version on the server, outdated apps keep calling the API
Bugs fixed in the app never reach the field

NODES.d: Ops adds a device of type TV to the restaurant with its serial number (device ID), name and orientation (0, 90, 180 or 270). This creates a restaurant device record and a TV record that the Screens page lists.
e: Serial number typed wrong, the app reports Device is not mapped
Same serial number still active under an old tenant or restaurant, the device keeps showing the old restaurant
Wrong restaurant menu on the TV
Orientation set differently from how the TV is mounted or from the playlist orientation
TV name left generic, operator cannot tell which physical screen is which
Content assigned to the wrong TV

NODES.d: The app authenticates as a device and calls the screen endpoint with its device ID, business and restaurant. The server looks for an active TV with that serial in that restaurant and returns not found otherwise, which the app shows as Device is not mapped.
e: The TV remains on Device is not mapped and cannot open the assigned board
Mapping message gives no device ID on screen to read out to support
Mapping only works after force stopping the app and clearing storage

NODES.d: Menu Boards > Playlists lists active playlists with total duration, thumbnails, the TVs each is live on, and Active or Inactive. Empty first-run state invites creating one.
e: Playlist with no active items is dropped from the listing because the query requires active items
Two playlists with the same name merge into one row in the listing
Listing does not paginate, large tenants load slowly

NODES.d: Create playlist: name (unique per restaurant, case insensitive) and orientation Landscape or Portrait. Orientation decides the board size later (1920 by 1080 or 1080 by 1920).
e: Orientation chosen does not match how the TV is mounted, boards render letterboxed with black bars
Duplicate name rejected only on save with Playlist name already exist
Orientation can be changed after boards are built, existing canvas boards keep their old size

NODES.d: Media items come from the content library with a duration each (HH:MM:SS). Type is taken from the file type (image or video).
e: Large video uploaded without compression, dongle stutters or runs out of memory
Codec the dongle cannot decode accepted in the playlist form
Duration of zero or a typo such as 10 minutes instead of 10 seconds accepted
Media file later deleted from the content library, TV shows a broken slide

NODES.d: A playlist can hold canvas boards (current editor) or older fixed menu templates (choose layout and items). Canvas items get a default 10 second duration.
e: Two content models live side by side, legacy templates and canvas boards render differently on the TV
Legacy template item rows are rebuilt by delete then insert outside a transaction, a failure leaves the template empty

NODES.d: Pick a fixed layout and the menus, categories and items to show. Item links are stored in the database and the TV re-reads names and prices live.
e: Menu block items not visible on the board though they are selected
Template insert swallows its error, the playlist saves with no template content and no message
Fixed templates cannot fit long menus, items cut off at the bottom

NODES.d: Drag to reorder. Nonvideo items allow 10 seconds through 23 hours, 59 minutes and 59 seconds. Videos use their own runtime. Duplicate inserts a separately named copy next to its source and assigns a distinct canvas identity. Save the playlist to publish changes.
e: New playlist with canvas boards only exists as a browser draft until the playlist form is saved, closing the tab loses the boards
Playlist update rolls back the name but item writes already happened outside the transaction
Sort order collisions after deletes make items play in an unexpected order

NODES.d: Full-page editor reached from the playlist form, with playlist, item, orientation and duration passed in page state. It loads the playlist, brand book, menus, modifiers and the image index.
e: A failed load is mistaken for a new blank canvas and the operator saves edits
The intended design may be replaced
Refreshing or deep-linking the editor loses page state and falls back to a hardcoded restaurant
Edits saved against the wrong restaurant
Board with background but no elements treated as not found

NODES.d: Board is 1920 by 1080 landscape or 1080 by 1920 portrait, set from the playlist orientation, with no later resize. Background is a colour, image, GIF or video (one video per board, background included).
e: Board aspect ratio differs from the TV panel, TV shows black bars on both sides
Background video plus foreground media exceed what the dongle can decode
No way to resize an existing board for a new TV, operator rebuilds it

NODES.d: Text with font role, weight, shadow, stroke and pill background; images with crop, mask and filters; video forced to autoplay, loop and mute; shapes, lines and freehand. Video must be MP4 under 100 MB.
e: H.264 codec check is disabled, a video the dongle cannot decode passes validation
Images up to 100 MB with no type check accepted, TV runs out of memory
Only one video allowed per board, paste or duplicate silently blocked
Text box grows past the board edge with no warning

NODES.d: Rotation snaps to right angles within 8 degrees, align and distribute, grouping, masks, layers panel with lock and hide, snapping to grid and edges.
e: Rotated element shifts position instead of rotating in place, and alignment is off between editor and TV
Flipped elements jump about 180 degrees while rotate-dragging
Circles are centre anchored while other shapes are not, aligning mixed shapes is off
Group moves together only when every member is selected

NODES.d: Pick one category's items from Menu Manager. Names, descriptions, prices, pictures, menu, category and item schedules and modifiers are copied into the board, then refreshed from live data at preview and on the TV.
e: A price looks correct in the editor and preview but shows zero on the mapped TV
Menu block items not visible on the TV though they show in the editor
Editing surface shows the stored copy, not live Menu Manager data, so price edits are invisible until preview
Item picker sometimes opens on the first tab with no items because of a loading race

NODES.d: Columns 1 to 10, price column width, price format and prefix, leader dots, show or hide names, prices, descriptions, pictures, column modifiers (sizes as columns) and row modifiers as inline text or pills with dividers. The standalone modifier block loads eligible top-level groups. Nested modifier names can appear disabled.
e: Narrowing a menu block that uses column modifiers wraps item names letter by letter and breaks the whole block
Prices are truncated with dots on the live board
Modifiers cannot be shown as menu items with descriptions, pill and pipe layouts break the design
Nested modifiers (modifier of a modifier) not supported in the menu block
Combo and build-your-own menus cannot be shown
Block grows to fit content and never shrinks, long descriptions push items off the board

NODES.d: Heading, Sub Heading and Paragraph roles from the Brand Book, Google or custom fonts. The brand book is copied into the board once; later changes need a manual sync.
e: Font fails to load silently, layout is measured with a fallback font and saved that way
Brand Book changes do not reach existing boards until each one is synced by hand
Custom font not available on the dongle, TV falls back to another font with different widths

NODES.d: The editor counts content nodes (elements plus every menu item part). At 500 or more it shows an advisory banner but saving is not blocked. No limit on JSON size.
e: Very large board saved with no hard limit, TV renders slowly or runs out of memory
Hidden elements still counted, warning appears on boards that are fine
Board JSON too large to save, the save fails and part of the screen stays blank

NODES.d: Autosave checks for changes every 30 seconds after initial loading. It skips an unchanged board and avoids an overlapping save. Canvas Save persists the design. Playlist Save is the publication step that notifies mapped devices. The editor also exposes Sync for TV for layouts that need updating.
e: Save fails and the raw error such as Request failed with status code 401 is shown, no retry except the next autosave
Two operators editing the same board, last save wins with no version check
Lost response then retry once created a duplicate board row (now matched by board ID)
Saving a canvas board does not invalidate the TV cache, the TV keeps the old board until another change or the cache expires
Edits not on TV for hours
Layout snapshot saved for the TV is measured in the operator browser, so browser and font differences travel to the TV

NODES.d: Preview (P key) renders the board full screen with the HTML renderer from the shared library and live menu data. It skips menu timing checks, which the TV applies.
e: Editing surface (canvas renderer) and preview (HTML renderer) lay text out differently
Layout differs between editor, preview and TV
Preview ignores menu timings, board looks full in preview but is empty on the TV outside the menu hours
Live data call fails and preview silently shows the stored copy

NODES.d: The Playlists page preview plays items in order with durations from the playlist preview data (up to 20 playlists at once).
e: Preview runs in a desktop browser, not at the TV resolution and fonts
Preview data built from the database differs from what the TV endpoint builds (different enrichment path)

NODES.d: Menu Boards > Screens lists the restaurant's active TVs by name with orientation, the playlists live now and status Live or Connected. Connected only means the TV exists, not that it is online.
e: Status shows Connected or Live without any heartbeat, an offline or dead dongle looks fine
App version and last seen time not shown
Empty state when Ops has not registered the TV yet, operator cannot add one themselves

NODES.d: Set playlist on a TV: pick playlists, order them; saving writes the TV playlist links and sort order and invalidates that TV's cache.
e: Playlist orientation not checked against the TV orientation
Adding playlists through the insert call does not invalidate the TV cache
New content late on the TV
Same playlist on many TVs, removing it from one changes nothing on the others as expected but operators expect global edits

NODES.t: Schedule playlists by day and time
NODES.d: Each TV and playlist pair has a default flag or a list of day schedules, all day or a start and end time. Schedules live on the TV link, not on the playlist.
e: Scheduling must be repeated on every TV, there is no schedule on the playlist itself
No playlist scheduled for the current time and no default, TV shows nothing
Overnight ranges past midnight and the restaurant time zone versus the dongle clock not handled clearly
Overlapping schedules have no stated priority

NODES.d: Playlist save or delete, TV playlist changes, device edits, business hours saves and Menu Manager publish clear the TV's cached screen data. The cached data otherwise lives 10 hours.
e: Canvas save, playlist link insert and some menu edits do not clear the cache, the TV serves stale data up to 10 hours
Old prices or boards on TV
Invalidation is fire and forget, a Redis failure is only logged
Menu Manager edits reach the TV only after the operator presses publish

NODES.t: TV app polls for screen data
NODES.d: The TV requests screen data, including playlists, board content, schedules and orientation. A fresh request can bypass the normal cached response. Poll timing, local cache and offline display depend on the deployed player.
e: Published change appears only after about 5 minutes, screensaver or board looks unchanged and staff clear the cache by hand
Any server error returns no data and the app shows a blank screen instead of the last good board
Playlists whose items fail to resolve are skipped silently
No push or MQTT channel for TVs, a TV cannot be told to refresh now

NODES.d: If the fetch fails the app shows its cached board or an offline message.
e: Board shows a blank screen with the offline message while Wi-Fi works
App does not fall back to the last cached board when offline
App stops opening until force stopped and storage cleared, also seen with other apps on the same dongle

NODES.d: The app uses business hours and the restaurant time zone to decide whether to show the board or a Restaurant Closed screen. Business hours saves clear the TV cache.
e: Boards show Restaurant Closed during open hours (old app version)
Split shifts or overnight hours misread at the boundary
Closed screen at the wrong time
Holiday closures and special hours not reflected

NODES.d: The app scales the 1920 by 1080 or 1080 by 1920 board to the panel and applies the TV orientation, using the saved layout snapshot for menu blocks.
e: Layout, spacing and font sizes differ from editor and preview
Black background on both sides after a system update, content not fitted to the TV size
Half of the screen blank because the board could not be saved fully
Prices truncated with dots on the TV
Rotated elements in a different position than in the editor

NODES.d: The TV hides menus, categories and items outside their Menu Manager visibility times, which were copied into the board. Preview does not do this.
e: Menu content disappears daily because menu timings are not set in Menu Manager
Empty board for part of the day
Every item must be set to all-day by hand for the board to show it
The mapped screen opens without displaying the menu
Timings changed in Menu Manager are not re-read, the board keeps the times copied at design

NODES.d: Compare the item, size, price and availability the guest sees on the TV with the same selection at the register. The screen service supplies stock information for linked items. The physical display determines what the guest actually sees.
e: Price on the board differs from POS price
Out of stock item still looks orderable
Text too small or low contrast from the queue
A board omits or obscures dietary information the restaurant intended to display
Guests need to ask staff for the missing information

NODES.d: The app loops items by duration, switches playlists by schedule and plays video, running unattended for many hours.
e: The menu board app closes abruptly during display
Memory grows over long runs with video and large images
Screensaver content does not refresh after a published update until the cache is cleared
No crash reporting or remote restart

NODES.d: Operator edits names, prices, descriptions, pictures or modifiers in Menu Manager and publishes. The TV re-reads them by ID on its next fetch; deleted items keep their stored copy.
e: Item deleted in Menu Manager keeps showing on the board from the stored copy
Guest asks for a removed item
New items are not added to a block automatically
Modifier lookup fails and stored modifier prices are kept

NODES.d: Staff mark an item out of stock at the register or in Menu Manager. Confirm the saved status, then check the same linked item on the TV after its screen data refreshes.
e: The register shows the item as sold out while the TV still shows the previous availability
Guests ask for an item the restaurant can no longer sell
The item is shown in an uploaded image on the playlist
The image can keep advertising the item after staff mark the menu item out of stock

NODES.d: Menu, category or item visibility times and business hours set in Menu Manager or Web Dash.
e: Menu timings left unset make the board empty outside the default window
Timings are copied into canvas boards at design, later changes need the board re-saved

NODES.d: Deleting an item soft deletes it; deleting the last item deactivates the playlist and unlinks it from every TV.
e: Deleting the last item silently deletes the playlist and blanks every TV using it
No undo or version history for boards

NODES.d: Soft deletes the playlist and its items, removes TV links and clears the caches of those TVs.
e: No warning which TVs will go blank
Schedules and settings of removed links left behind

NODES.d: Ops edits or deletes the TV device; the TV record is hard deleted and its cache cleared. Moving a dongle means deleting and re-registering it.
e: Device left mapped to an old tenant after a move, shows the old restaurant's menu
Deleting a TV leaves its schedules and links behind
Dongle reused at another site keeps cached content offline

NODES.d: Module switched off or tenant churns; devices should be unmapped and recovered.
e: Dongles keep showing the last cached board after churn

NOTES: The Android POS app submits stock changes. Refresh timing, offline fallback, closed screen behaviour and how the TV renders stock require verification on the separate TV player.

Canvas Save persists a draft. Playlist Save notifies mapped devices and invalidates their screen data. The normal screen cache lasts up to ten hours, and a fresh request can bypass it. The player refresh interval requires device verification.
Canvas boards copy menu, category and item schedules at design time; the TV applies them, the Web Dash preview does not. This matches PROD-4784 and 4659.
Device registration is assumed to happen in the Ops dashboard device screens (TV device type with serial and orientation); there is no self-serve pairing code in Web Dash.
No heartbeat, last-seen or app version reporting for TVs was found; Screens status Live or Connected is derived from playlist links only.
PROD 4807 records a partly blank board and a save failure. The ticket does not establish a maximum supported document size.
The Node.js CVE tickets that list Menu Boards (4997, 5002) are infrastructure and not attached.
Zeus internal, 02473c3bac9. See CanvasEditor/index.tsx, playlistItemDuration.ts, menuModifierAdapter.ts and menu-board/playlist and screen services.
